advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Do not blanket-ignore `assume_role_policy` drift on `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin` (sole execute-api:Invoke grantee); this disables detection of trust-policy tampering on a security boundary.
evidence: opcert.tf:11-12: role `rebar-opcert-admin` … the SOLE grantee of `execute-api:Invoke`
opcert.tf:145: `assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.opcert_admin_assume.json` — the trust policy is fully HCL-owned, not an out-of-band secret
Comment's own stated risk (opcert.tf:151-152) is 'masking real drift'; this guard itself masks real trust-policy drift on the most security-sensitive resource in the file
opcert.tf:21-30: `variable "opcert_admin_principal_arns"` … `default = []` (empty by default so the role trusts nobody)
opcert.tf:149: comment confirms drift runs `terraform plan` with no -var
advisory.finding: `ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy]` on `aws_iam_role.opcert_admin` permanently blinds Terraform drift detection to changes in the trust policy of the role that is the SOLE grantee of `execute-api:Invoke`. Out-of-band tampering that adds an attacker principal to the trust list will never be flagged by the daily drift sweep the comment claims to protect.
merged_from: The phantom drift's root cause is that the terraform-drift workflow runs `terraform plan` with no `-var`, so `opcert_admin_principal_arns` defaults to `[]`; the correct IaC fix is to supply the deploy value to the plan (a committed non-secret `.tfvars`/`TF_VAR_opcert_admin_principal_arns` in .github/workflows/terraform-drift.yml) rather than adding `ignore_changes` that hides real drift going forward.
scenarios: An operator or attacker edits the role trust policy in the AWS console to add a foreign principal; the daily drift sweep stays green and never surfaces it.
A legitimate principal ARN is accidentally removed out-of-band; Terraform never reconciles it back.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconsider `test_terraform_opcert_admin_role_ignores_assume_role_policy_drift`; it pins drift-blindness on the trust policy under a false analogy to the secret SSM key's ignore_changes=[value].
evidence: test file lines 121-124: '(mirroring the operator-seeded key param's ignore_changes = [value])'
opcert.tf:48-59: the key param ignores `value` because the operator SEEDS the real key out-of-band (a secret placeholder CHANGEME)
opcert.tf:145: assume_role_policy is derived from HCL `data.aws_iam_policy_document.opcert_admin_assume.json`, not an out-of-band secret
opcert.tf:66-74: the origin-guard param deliberately carries NO ignore_changes because it is Terraform-managed — same reasoning argues the HCL-owned trust policy should NOT be ignored
advisory.finding: The added comment and test justify the guard as 'the SAME operator-owned pattern as the key SSM param', but the analogy is false: the SSM key ignores a secret VALUE placeholder Terraform never manages, whereas `assume_role_policy` is fully defined in HCL from a variable. This mismatched rationale is baked into a regression test that will now lock in the drift-blindness.
scenarios: The regression test cements ignore_changes=[assume_role_policy] as a contract, making it harder to later restore drift detection on the trust boundary.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the drift-check root cause (pass the deploy -var / tfvars for opcert_admin_principal_arns to the terraform-drift plan) instead of adding `ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy]`, which permanently disables drift detection on the admin role's trust boundary.
evidence: opcert.tf:143-145 role `rebar-opcert-admin` with `assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.opcert_admin_assume.json` — the trust boundary
opcert.tf:163-165 comment: this role's inline policy is 'The ONLY policy in this IaC that grants execute-api:Invoke ... rebar-opcert-admin is the single principal that can call the API'
terraform-drift.yml:1-5 the drift check's stated purpose: FAILS 'when ... live infra that has drifted from HCL' — ignore_changes on assume_role_policy defeats this for the trust list

ABSENCE: unlike aws_ssm_parameter.opcert_ed25519_key whose `value` is a `CHANGEME` placeholder never modeled in HCL (opcert.tf:52-59), assume_role_policy IS fully rendered from var.opcert_admin_principal_arns in HCL (opcert.tf:132-145), so the 'same operator-owned pattern' analogy does not hold
advisory.finding: `ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy]` on aws_iam_role.opcert_admin permanently blinds the terraform-drift sweep to any out-of-band modification of the admin role's trust policy — the very trust boundary that controls who may assume the SOLE execute-api:Invoke grantee. An attacker or errant operator who adds a principal to the trust list will never be detected or reverted by drift detection.
scenarios: An operator or attacker with iam:UpdateAssumeRolePolicy adds their own ARN to rebar-opcert-admin's trust policy out-of-band; the daily drift sweep stays green and the addition is never surfaced.
A misconfiguration widens the trust list (e.g. account root) after deploy; Terraform never reconciles it back.
advisory.suggested_fix: Remove the `ignore_changes = [assume_role_policy]` lifecycle block and instead give var.opcert_admin_principal_arns a committed default (or supply a -var-file) so `terraform plan` with no -var renders the same principals as the applied state, eliminating the phantom diff without blinding drift detection on the trust policy.
